note: Three open chords put in time in three sections that change one thing each: the shapes alone, one strum a bar with three beats to move, then a strum on every beat with the eyes on the lit chord box instead of the hand (folded in from guitar-beginner-g-c-and-d-without-looking, whose faster tempo is the moves' range). Each step says the control, what it starts, the beat to strum on and the beat to move on; the key is the lesson, so only the tempo moves.

exercise.title: G, C and D in time
exercise.why: A change is in time when the new chord sounds on beat 1, so your fingers have to start moving one beat earlier, on beat 4.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Each box shows where the fingers go, and the number on a dot is the finger to use.
Fret G and strum it once, then C, then D, then G again, slowly.
Practice until every string rings in each chord.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down once on beat 1, then use beats 2, 3 and 4 to move your fingers to the next chord.
If a change comes late, keep counting and catch the next beat 1.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Strum down on every beat, one bar for each chord, and start moving your fingers to the next chord on beat 4. Watch the lit chord box instead of your hand.
Practice until the changes are in your muscle memory: the new chord sounds on beat 1 with no gap, and your hand finds it without you looking.
